scope: UI-only persisted schedule authorization entry and shared browser scope editor integration; fake Control list responses and fake desktop bridge in React happy-dom tests
entry: 日程安排 → 日期中的日程卡或随时手动执行列表 → 浏览器授权
changes: Shared AutomationSkillStatus renders the entry for scheduled and manual Skill cards containing browser mutation tool refs.
Authorization uses the saved definition thread, immutable Skill ref, saved approval mode, and saved parameter names.
Opening a card never grants access; the user explicitly authorizes or revokes through BrowserExecutionAuthorization.
Scoped-only Skills require an explicitly configured valid scope and cannot choose per-action authorization.
Authority changes reset the entry; re-opening reads current bridge status instead of retaining an authorized claim.
Legacy prompt schedules and read-only Skills retain their existing layout.

pauseResumeFinding.conclusion: The current Control API/client/runtime has no individual schedule update, pause, or resume operation. Legacy app-server automation/update is a separate compatibility path and cannot be attached to current Control schedules.

limitations: This evidence does not prove manual desktop use, real browser grant execution, model execution, schedule timing, or file delivery.
Browser scope is explicitly configured in the UI and is not persisted in SkillInvocation or the schedule definition; after restart it must be configured and authorized again.
Full UI/build/browser layout verification is coordinated by the root integration task.
